newsitem.title: USA: US bond market trend seen bullish in 97 - Prudential.
newsitem.headline: US bond market trend seen bullish in 97 - Prudential.

text.p: The U.S. bond market is likely to remain in a bullish trend in 1997, with yields dropping as low as close to 6.0 percent in the long end of the curve, said Prudential Securities chief economist Richard Rippe.

"I'm optimistic on the bond market," Rippe told reporters at Prudential's year-end economic outlook conference. "I see bond yields in the vicinity of 6.0 percent in 1997," the Prudential chief economist added.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was quoted off 7/32 at 100-8/32 by late morning on Tuesday to yield 6.48 percent.
Rippe said there are five main reasons why he thinks the U.S. Treasury market will be a good investment opportunity in 1997. They are:
-- a modestly restrictive monetary policy by the Federal Reserve
-- the possibility of a budget deal between Democrats and Republicans in the U.S.
-- moderate growth in developed foreign economies
Rippe's outlook for 1997 envisions a U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 2.1 percent against an estimated 2.3 percent growth in 1996.

He believes the consumer price index will rise by 3.2 percent next year against an estimated 2.9 percent in 1996. The economist said, however, he believes there's "room for improvement" on the inflation front.
Rippe see the joblessness rate staying at an average of 5.3 percent in 1997 against a projected 5.4 percent average for the current year.
The economist said he sees the Fed on hold for "a considerable time," adding he believes that current monetary policy is mildly restrictive.
